statement_refuted: There is a universal finite bound on M=sup_b ||p_{Q3|Qrest=b}||_infinity after splitting off three large spectral directions and conditioning only on the scalar complementary quadratic form Qrest.
construction: Take independent cap-one X1,X3,X4 uniform on [0,1], X2 uniform-density indicator on m separated intervals [10k,10k+1/m]. Let S=(X1+X2)/sqrt(2), D=(X1-X2)/sqrt(2), Q3=D^2+X3^2-X4^2, Qrest=S^2. Then Q=X1^2+X2^2+X3^2-X4^2 is diagonal and has full density <=pi.
exact_lower_bound: At b_m=1/(2m^2), D|(Qrest=b_m) is uniform on [-1/(sqrt(2)m),1/(sqrt(2)m)], and p_{Q3|Qrest=b_m}(0) >= 0.5*(log(sqrt(2)m)+1), hence M diverges.
mechanism: Scalar conditioning can squeeze one of the three core directions to O(1/m), leaving the opposite-sign rank-two logarithmic singularity regularized only at scale m^-2. Averaging over Qrest is essential and the worst conditional core discards that smoothing.
scope_note: This is not a counterexample to QFORM. The full form is diagonal and satisfies the proved pi bound. It refutes only the proposed scalar worst-condition proof interface.
replacement_obligation: Control the shifted mixture E_{Qrest}[p_{Q3|Qrest}(t-Qrest)] directly or aggregate original-coordinate product structure before worst-case conditioning; do not replace it by sup_b of conditional core densities.
